title: Choose Deck's layout
question: Same Swiss Grid world in sun yellow, three ways to lay out a slide editor. The roll dealt the talk timeline. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Talk timeline
options.lineage: The suite's numbered strip, laid along time
options.thesis: The slides run as numbered blocks along a timeline under the canvas, each as wide as the time you plan to spend on it, with the notes beside the slide.
options.viewport: Sun rail, a bar reading Deck / Paperlight launch talk with Present and Save, the slide on the 72px canvas, speaker notes on the right, and a 7-slide timeline totalling 5:30.
options.risk: Planned times are a new idea to learn, and many short slides make narrow blocks.

options.label: Outline and slide
options.lineage: Write the talk, the slides follow
options.thesis: A numbered outline of every slide's title and points sits on the left and edits like a document; the slide it describes is drawn live on the right.
options.viewport: Sun rail, the command bar, a 440px numbered outline with the caret in slide 03, the slide on the canvas and speaker notes under it.
options.risk: There are no thumbnails, so you see slide layouts only one at a time.

options.label: Continuous sheet
options.lineage: The deck as one long page
options.thesis: Slides stack down one scrolling sheet at working size, numbered in the margin, each with its notes beside it, so you edit the whole talk in place.
options.viewport: Sun rail, the command bar, then slides 02 to 04 down the ruled canvas with 03 outlined in ink and its notes on the right.
options.risk: Only one slide and a half show at a time, and reordering needs the sorter.
